rows: Stationary: $f\prime(c)=0$. Interior critical input: $f(c)$ exists and $f\prime(c)=0$ or $f\prime(c)$ does not exist. These are candidates, not classifications.

On an interval: $f\prime>0$ gives strict increase; $f\prime<0$ gives strict decrease; $f\prime\ge0$ gives nondecrease. Require differentiability inside and continuity at included endpoints. Do not bridge a domain gap.
At continuous interior candidate $c$, neighbouring derivative signs $+\to-$ give a local maximum; $-\to+$ a local minimum; unchanged nonzero signs give neither.

$f\prime\prime>0$: slopes increase, concave up. $f\prime\prime<0$: slopes decrease, concave down. Inflection: change of concavity through a continuous graph point. $f\prime\prime(c)=0$ alone is insufficient.
$f\prime(c)=0$; $f$ differentiable nearby; $f\prime\prime(c)$ exists. Positive: local minimum; negative: local maximum; zero: inconclusive.
Continuous $f$ on closed bounded $[a,b]$ attains maximum and minimum. Compare all interior critical values and both endpoint values. Keep ties. A limiting value need not be attained.

Choose a model and signed rates; identify fixed quantities. Differentiate with respect to the common time before inserting instantaneous values. Chain/product rules retain every changing factor. Check units and validity.

$A=ab:\ \dot A=b\dot a+a\dot b$. $d^2=x^2+y^2:\ d\dot d=x\dot x+y\dot y$. Fixed-radius sphere: $V=\pi h^2(R-h/3)$, $\dot V=\pi h(2R-h)\dot h$, $0<h<2R$. Constant $pV:\ V\dot p+p\dot V=0$ (absolute pressure).
Continuous on $[a,b]$, differentiable on $(a,b)$, $a<b$:$${f\prime(c)=\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}},\quad a<c<b.$$ At least one match; not necessarily unique or at the midpoint.
$f\prime=0\Rightarrow f$ constant; $f\prime=g\prime\Rightarrow f-g$ constant. With MVT hypotheses, $m\le f\prime\le M$ gives $m(b-a)\le f(b)-f(a)\le M(b-a)$.
Function/domain ≠ sample list ≠ displayed line. Record spacing and limits. Separate domain components. Check derivative evidence. Finite sampling cannot generally certify every feature.

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
x = np.linspace(0, 1, 401)  # endpoints included; 400 gaps
y = x + 0.08 * np.sin(20 * np.pi * x)  # radians
plt.plot(x, y, "o-")       # markers plus connecting segments
plt.xlim(0, 1); plt.ylim(-0.15, 1.15)
plt.xlabel("x (dimensionless)"); plt.ylabel("f(x) (dimensionless)")
plt.show()
# Change n in linspace to change samples; limits change the view.
# For a domain gap, plot the two component arrays separately.
notation: Notation: primes refer to the displayed input; dots to time. $a,b$ denote endpoints or panel sides as labelled; $c$ an interior input; $R$ a fixed radius; $h$ depth; $p$ absolute pressure; $V$ volume. A rate has output units per input unit.
